title: 当 27 亿人的会议没有中美：安提瓜峰会重新定价「中等强国」的多边筹码
summary: 第 28 届英联邦政府首脑会议 11 月 1 日至 4 日在安提瓜和巴布达举行。56 个成员国、约 27 亿人口，却是一个美国与中国都不在场的论坛。在关税被武器化、大型峰会连联合声明都难以产出的年份，这场「小国办大会」真正测试的，是中等规模多边机制还能不能交付可执行的成果。
body: 2026 年 11 月 1 日至 4 日，第 28 届英联邦政府首脑会议（CHOGM）在安提瓜和巴布达首都圣约翰举行。据英联邦秘书处，这是该组织成立以来由面积最小的国家承办的一次峰会，东道主在会议前夕刚迎来独立 45 周年。56 个成员国合计约 27 亿人口，接近全球人口三分之一，而会场所在的加勒比小岛人口不足十万。
这场会议之所以值得放到全球治理的坐标系里看，不在于它的规模，而在于它是少数几个既没有美国、也没有中国参与的多边领导人论坛之一；在一个大国协调失灵、关税与供应链被反复当作施压工具的年份，一个共识型组织能否把议程从表态推进到机制，本身就是一次可观察的压力测试。
## 一份刻意「去宏大化」的议程
本届主题是「加速伙伴关系与投资，共建繁荣英联邦」。秘书处为领导人列出的正式优先项只有三条：清除成员国之间贸易壁垒的工作计划、基于脆弱性指标的可持续债务与优惠融资共同平台，以及面向 2027 年的投资战略。外长会先行，小国部长级会议并行，领导人环节以仅限政府首脑参加的闭门退修会收尾。
会前公布的投资平台更能说明务实取向：20 个发展中成员国提交了 60 多个被标记为「高影响力」的可投资项目，合计规模据称超过 300 亿美元。加拿大政府披露其对英联邦成员国贸易额已逾 1000 亿美元；秘书处另计划设立基金，为约 1000 万青年提供数字技能培训。这些数字都不惊人，但共同指向一件事——把「合作」拆成可签约、可融资、可验收的具体条目。
## 关税外溢，把「内部循环」从口号变成对冲工具
英联邦秘书长 Shirley Botchwey 在会前对美联社的表述，几乎为整场峰会定了调：「所有国家一觉醒来就被加了关税。如果我们在彼此之间贸易得更多，那么英联邦之外发生什么，就不会太剧烈地影响这些国家。」她把冲突、经济冲击、生活成本上升、气候变化与「关税武器化」并列，称这些压力最终都落在普通人的口袋里。
> 「我们面对的是冲突、经济冲击、成本上升、气候变化、贸易、关税的武器化，而这一切直接打到民众的钱包上。」——英联邦秘书长 Shirley Botchwey，会前接受美联社采访

这段话的背景是：特朗普政府对其贸易伙伴加征了自大萧条以来最高水平的进口关税，税率又因法律挑战而反复波动。对 56 个以中小经济体为主、且多数曾依附于同一套殖民贸易体系的国家而言，降低彼此间的制度性交易成本，就不只是发展议题，而是一种风险对冲。加拿大总理卡尼把出席峰会定位为贸易多元化与「中等强国战略」的一次测试；国际贸易律师 Barry Appleton 也将其解读为「在没有美国在场的场合推进新外交政策」的机会。
## 记忆政治与交易政治的正面碰撞
真正让会场气氛复杂的，是议程之外的赔偿正义议题。加共体赔偿委员会把本届称为「赔偿 CHOGM」，加勒比多国政府要求把奴隶制赔偿从边缘推向中心。据 CNN 与《牙买加拾穗者报》，秘书处认为讨论时机已到；但白金汉宫方面释放的信号是，查尔斯三世 11 月 3 日的开幕致辞会以「诚实与遗憾」谈及过去最不光彩的篇章，却不作正式道歉，重心仍放在共同挑战的务实解法上。
主办方的口径更谨慎：安提瓜和巴布达赔偿支持委员会主席 Dorbrene O'Marde 表示，CHOGM 正式日程内并未安排具体赔偿活动。先例也并不乐观——2024 年萨摩亚峰会上，倡导者未能争取到议程空间，但最终仍形成了一份 56 国共同签署的声明。换句话说，这条线索衡量的是组织的规范生产能力，而不是一次会议能否给出赔偿方案。
## 缺席者的在场，与小国的议程杠杆
澳大利亚广播公司把 CHOGM 描述为少数没有美中出席的多边论坛之一，但「缺席」并不等于「无关」：该报道同时指出，中国二十年间在加勒比投入数十亿美元基础设施，安提瓜的主要港口、机场，乃至承办峰会活动的板球场，都带有中资背景。卡塔尔、科威特、巴林、巴西与阿联酋也派官员与会。大国不在桌前，却始终在桌面的投影里。
对照更能说明问题：同期在亚特兰大举行的 G20 外长会未能产出联合声明。规模更小、共享制度习惯与议事语言的组织，反而更容易形成共识文本——这是「中等规模多边主义」被低估的优势。而 56 个成员国中有 49 个临海，海平面上升与债务脆弱性对它们不是抽象议题；小国的杠杆不在投票权重，而在于把自身生存条件写成议程，并把议程转化为规范与融资工具。
## 该用什么标尺判断成败
- 11 月 4 日闭幕成果文件是否明确背书贸易壁垒工作计划、可持续债务平台与 2027 投资战略，还是停留在原则性表述。
- Jumby Bay 岛领导人闭门退修会，是否为赔偿议题给出任何可延续的讨论框架，哪怕只是程序性安排。
- 出席率本身：哪些国家派政府首脑、哪些改派部长，是观察组织凝聚力的直接指标。
- 11 月 9 日至 20 日安塔利亚 COP31 上，安提瓜形成的债务与气候融资措辞会不会被沿用，这是成果能否外溢的关键检验。
## 结语：从公报长度转向机制密度
对这类论坛最常见的误判，是拿 G7、G20 的曝光度去衡量它。安提瓜峰会更像一次制度实验：当大国协调成本升高，覆盖 27 亿人口、以共识为运作方式的中型组织，能否用一份可执行的贸易工作计划、一套按脆弱性分配优惠融资的平台，以及一条面向 2027 的投资管道，证明「小多边」仍有公共品供给能力。真正值得记录的不是公报写了多少段，而是三年后这些机制是否还在运转。

title: A Summit for 2.7 Billion Without the US or China: What Antigua Really Tests
summary: The 28th Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting runs from 1 to 4 November 2026 in St John's, Antigua and Barbuda. It gathers 56 member states and roughly 2.7 billion people, yet neither Washington nor Beijing is in the room. In a year when tariffs are weaponised and larger summits struggle to agree on a communiqué, the real question is whether a mid-sized consensus body can still deliver executable outcomes.
body: The 28th Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) convenes in St John's, Antigua and Barbuda, from 1 to 4 November 2026. According to the Commonwealth Secretariat, it is the smallest country ever to host the biennial summit, and the host marked the 45th anniversary of its independence on the eve of the meeting. The 56 member states represent about 2.7 billion people, close to a third of humanity, while the island itself has fewer than 100,000 residents.

The summit deserves a place in any assessment of global governance not because of its size, but because it is one of the few multilateral leaders' forums attended by neither the United States nor China. In a year of faltering great-power coordination, with tariffs and supply chains repeatedly used as instruments of pressure, whether a consensus-based organisation can move its agenda from declaration to mechanism is itself an observable stress test.
## An agenda deliberately stripped of grandeur

The theme is 'Accelerating Partnerships and Investment for a Prosperous Commonwealth'. The Secretariat listed just three formal priorities for leaders: a work programme on removing barriers to intra-Commonwealth trade, a common platform on sustainable debt and concessional funding indexed to vulnerability, and an investment strategy for 2027. Foreign ministers meet first, a ministerial meeting on small states runs in parallel, and the leaders' sessions close with a restricted retreat on Jumby Bay Island.

The investment platform unveiled before the summit makes the pragmatism concrete: 20 developing member countries submitted more than 60 'high impact', investment-ready projects representing over US$30 billion. Canada's government says its trade with Commonwealth partners already exceeds US$100 billion, and the Secretariat plans a fund to deliver digital skills to roughly 10 million young adults. None of these figures is startling, but all of them convert 'cooperation' into items that can be signed, financed and audited.
## Tariff spillover turns intra-bloc trade into a hedge

Commonwealth Secretary-General Shirley Botchwey set the tone in remarks to the Associated Press before the meeting: 'All the countries woke up one day and were slapped with tariffs. If we are trading more among ourselves, whatever happens outside the Commonwealth will not affect countries too much.' She grouped conflict, economic shocks, rising costs, climate change and the weaponisation of tariffs together, arguing that all of them land directly in people's pockets.

> 'We're looking at issues like conflict, economic shocks, rising costs, climate change, trade, weaponization of tariffs; and all of this hitting directly the pockets of our people.' — Shirley Botchwey, Commonwealth Secretary-General, speaking to the Associated Press

The backdrop is the highest US import duties on trading partners since the Great Depression, imposed under President Donald Trump and fluctuating amid legal challenges. For 56 mostly small and mid-sized economies, many of them shaped by a shared colonial trading system, cutting institutional transaction costs among themselves is not merely a development question but a form of risk hedging. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney framed the trip as a test of trade diversification and middle-power strategy, while trade lawyer Barry Appleton called it an opportunity to advance a new foreign policy 'with the U.S. not present'.
## When the politics of memory meets the politics of transaction

What complicates the room is an item outside the formal agenda: reparatory justice. The CARICOM Reparations Commission has dubbed this the 'reparations CHOGM', and Caribbean governments want the issue moved from the margins to the centre. CNN and the Jamaica Gleaner reported that the Secretary-General believes the time has come to discuss it, while Buckingham Palace signalled that King Charles III's opening address on 3 November would address the most shameful aspects of the past with honesty and sorrow but stop short of a formal apology.

Local organisers were more cautious. Dorbrene O'Marde, chair of Antigua and Barbuda's Reparations Support Commission, said no specific reparation activities were scheduled within CHOGM itself. Precedent is mixed: advocates failed to secure agenda space at the 2024 summit in Samoa, yet that meeting still produced a statement signed by all 56 members. The thread therefore measures the organisation's capacity to produce norms, not its ability to settle a claim in one sitting.
## Absence as presence, and the leverage of small states

ABC News described CHOGM as one of the few multilateral forums without the US or China, but absence is not irrelevance. The same reporting noted that China has spent billions on Caribbean infrastructure over two decades, including Antigua's main port, its airport and the cricket ground hosting summit events. Officials from Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Brazil and the United Arab Emirates also attended. The great powers are not at the table, but their shadow stays on it.

The contrast is instructive: a G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta ended without a joint statement. A smaller body with shared institutional habits and a common procedural language may find a consensus communiqué easier to reach — an underrated advantage of mid-sized multilateralism. And because 49 of the Commonwealth's 56 countries border the ocean, rising seas and debt vulnerability are not abstractions. Small states wield leverage less through voting weight than by writing their own survival conditions into the agenda and converting them into norms and financing instruments.
## What to measure
- Whether the closing outcome on 4 November endorses the trade work programme, the sustainable debt platform and the 2027 investment strategy, or settles for principles.
- Whether the Jumby Bay leaders' retreat produces any continuing framework for discussing reparatory justice, even a procedural one.
- Attendance itself: which governments send heads of government and which send ministers is a direct read on cohesion.
- Whether the debt and climate-finance language from Antigua survives into COP31 in Antalya, scheduled for 9 to 20 November — the clearest test of whether the outcomes travel.
## Conclusion: from communiqué length to mechanism density

The common mistake is to judge such forums by the visibility of the G7 or G20. Antigua is closer to an institutional experiment: when great-power coordination grows expensive, can a consensus-based organisation covering 2.7 billion people still supply public goods — an executable trade work programme, a vulnerability-indexed financing platform, an investment pipeline through 2027? What will matter is not how many paragraphs the communiqué runs, but whether those mechanisms are still operating three years from now.

Anjo, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons; figure 2, the 2018 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting, courtesy of the UK Foreign and Commonwealth Office, CC BY 2.0. Facts and quotations are drawn from public reporting by the Commonwealth Secretariat, the Associated Press, ABC News and CTV News; the source link is appended below.

title: 开源不再只是分发方式：乌镇峰会透露的 AI 竞争「换赛道」信号
summary: 2026 年世界互联网大会乌镇峰会以「开源开放 共建共享」为主题，混元 Hy4 preview 发布即全面开源，全球主流大模型调用榜前六全部来自中国团队。但更值得读的信号是：当基础模型变得容易获取，竞争正从模型本身外移到算力底座、开发工具、行业方案与服务生态，而开源的另一面是一张需要协同支付的安全账单。
body: 以「开源开放 共建共享——携手构建网络空间命运共同体」为主题的 2026 年世界互联网大会乌镇峰会已于 11 月初启幕。据新华社报道，腾讯在「互联网之光」博览会现场展示的混元 Hy4 preview 大模型发布即全面开源，面向软件工程、科研攻关与智能办公等生产力场景；峰会还首次设置「人工智能乌镇对话」，并打造开源主题生态体验馆。
如果只看「又开源了一个模型」，会错过这届峰会真正的行业信号：多位与会嘉宾判断，基础模型供给变得更容易获取之后，竞争赛道正在向外延伸，算力底座、开发工具、行业方案与服务生态成为新的比拼阵地。换言之，开源已经从一种分发策略，变成了重组产业分工的组织方式。
## 从「发布即开源」到一整套开源基础设施
本届峰会重点打造的开源主题生态体验馆里，之江实验室 021 科学基础模型、魔搭社区（杭州）开发者中心等标志性成果集中亮相，六大领域的国家人工智能应用中试基地同时登场。这些不是单个模型，而是模型之外的数据、工具链、评测与中试环境——恰恰是「赛道外移」所指的那一层。

中国互联网络信息中心政策与国际合作所发布的《生成式人工智能应用发展报告（2026）》给出了另一个坐标：深度求索、月之暗面等本土企业先后发布多个万亿级参数开源大模型，全球主流大模型调用榜单上排名前六的模型全部来自中国团队。官方表述中，中国在开源模型下载量、衍生模型数等关键指标上保持领先。11 月 2 日揭晓的 2026 年世界互联网大会领先科技奖共 20 项成果，涵盖「九章四号」光量子计算原型机、面向空间量子信息的光传输技术、面向物理 AI 的整车智能体技术平台等前沿方向。
## 为什么开源在智能体时代更关键
中国工程院外籍院士、清华大学智能产业研究院创始院长张亚勤给出了一个简洁的因果链：「开源开放，本就是互联网的根基。开放催生海量数据，成为大模型的燃料，步入智能体时代，开源开放的价值更为关键。」阿里巴巴集团董事会主席蔡崇信的表述则更偏向普及逻辑：「只有开源才能普及，只有普及才能创造可持续、普惠的智能时代。」
> 「开源有可能扩大一些综合的安全问题，深度求索目前正在通过模型分级等方式，对开源模型在某些方面的能力进行限制，以提升安全性。」——深度求索研究工程师高熙，乌镇峰会期间公开表述

博览会现场的一个案例把这条链路讲得很具体：搭载蚂蚁灵波 LingBot 模型的机器人已能在模拟零售药房场景中抓取不同包装的药品，并在上海浦东多家药房投入应用；该系列模型已支持 17 个品牌、20 多种不同构型的机器人，而用户在调试和使用中反馈的数据，会反哺模型迭代。这里真正稀缺的已不是权重文件，而是「部署—反馈—再训练」的闭环，以及让不同构型硬件共用一套智能的工程能力。本届博览会以「智能互联、智见未来」为主题，来自 54 个国家和地区的 671 家企业带来 1000 余项新技术新产品。
## 开源的另一面：一张需要协同支付的安全账单
11 月 3 日主论坛发布的《前沿人工智能安全与治理 2026：风险认知与协同治理》报告，把讨论从原则推到机制。报告由世界互联网大会人工智能专业委员会发布，提出五点建议：推动模型安全评测协同、做好不同主体安全承诺及落实情况的协同核验、加强风险事件通报与联合处置、完善智能体和开放模型的协同治理安排、深化能力建设合作以普惠共享安全与治理资源。

值得注意的是报告对「前沿人工智能」的界定方式：以能力水平作为判定标准，不设置参数量、训练算力等硬性门槛，把智能体、多智能体协作、具身智能系统一并纳入，并聚焦非军事领域的规模化应用。研究指出，滥用与犯罪风险、信息完整性风险、关键系统风险已持续显现并转化为现实危害；社会认知与结构风险在就业、教育领域长期累积。相应地，产业侧也在给出工具：深度求索谈模型分级以限制开源模型的部分能力，MiniMax 首席架构师冯雯则指出，开源模型防御能力在网络攻击场景中不断提升，未来可通过部署开源模型增强整体防御。同一份开放性，既是风险扩散面，也是防御基础设施。
## 从共识到可复制方案
峰会期间发布的「携手构建网络空间命运共同体」精品案例，从 80 余个国家和地区 360 余项申报中遴选 11 项实践样本，覆盖网络安全、跨境数据可信治理、开源协作等方向。腾讯集团高级副总裁奚丹把价值判断说得更直白：「发展人工智能，核心就是要把人的价值和作用放大，让人工智能成就人。」全球移动通信系统协会董事长约翰·霍夫曼则重申峰会一贯宗旨——「不让任何一个人掉队」。
- 判断开源成效的指标应从下载量、星标数，转向衍生模型数、行业渗透率与真实部署回流量。
- 模型分级、评测协同与风险事件通报，正在成为开源生态的「制度性接口」，其重要性不亚于许可证文本。
- 算力供不应求仍是过去一年的硬约束：当模型权重免费，算力、数据与工程能力反而更集中地决定竞争格局。
- 治理成果若只停留在报告，难以约束跨境部署；能否沉淀为可复制方案，是下一阶段的分水岭。
## 结语：稀缺性正在上移
把这几条线索放在一起看，乌镇峰会传递的不是「我们又开源了」，而是价值链的重新定价：基础模型加速商品化，稀缺性上移到算力底座、工具链、行业方案、服务生态与安全治理。对开发者与企业而言，真正的门槛不再是能否拿到一个足够强的模型，而是能否把它放进一条可运营、可评测、可追责的生产链路。这也解释了为什么一届以「开源」为主题的峰会，会把同样多的篇幅留给治理报告。

title: Open Source Is No Longer Just a Distribution Channel: Wuzhen and AI's Changing Race
summary: The 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit is built around open source and openness. Tencent's Hunyuan Hy4 preview was released fully open, and the top six models on a leading global LLM usage ranking all come from Chinese teams. But the more consequential signal is that once foundation models become easy to obtain, competition shifts outward to compute infrastructure, developer tooling, vertical solutions and service ecosystems — while open source simultaneously presents a security bill that has to be paid collectively.
body: The 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit opened in early November under the theme 'Open Source and Openness, Joint Contribution and Shared Benefits'. According to Xinhua, Tencent displayed its newly released Hunyuan Hy4 preview model at the Light of Internet Expo, fully open-sourced at launch and targeted at software engineering, scientific research and intelligent office work. The summit also introduced an 'AI Wuzhen Dialogue' and a dedicated open-source ecosystem pavilion.

Reading this as 'one more model went open' would miss the industry signal. Several participants argued that as foundation model supply becomes easier to access, the competitive frontier is moving outward — toward compute infrastructure, developer tooling, vertical solutions and service ecosystems. Open source has ceased to be merely a distribution strategy and is becoming a way of reorganising the division of labour across the industry.
## From open-at-launch to a full open-source stack

The pavilion showcased more than models: the Zhejiang Lab 021 scientific foundation model, the ModelScope community's Hangzhou developer centre, and national AI application pilot bases across six domains. These are the data, toolchains, evaluation environments and pilot infrastructure that sit around a model — precisely the layer the 'outward shift' refers to.

A report from the Policy and International Cooperation Institute at the China Internet Network Information Centre, the 'Generative AI Application Development Report (2026)', offers a second coordinate: domestic firms including DeepSeek and Moonshot AI have released multiple trillion-parameter open models, and all six top-ranked models on a major global LLM usage leaderboard come from Chinese teams. Official accounts say China leads on open-model downloads and derivative model counts. On 2 November, 20 projects received the summit's 2026 Leading Science and Technology Awards, spanning the 'Jiuzhang IV' photonic quantum computing prototype, space quantum information transmission, and a vehicle-level agent platform for physical AI.
## Why openness matters more in the agent era

Zhang Yaqin, a foreign member of the Chinese Academy of Engineering and founding dean of Tsinghua's Institute for AI Industry Research, offered a compact causal chain: 'Open source and openness are the very foundation of the internet. Openness generates massive data, which becomes the fuel for large models; as we enter the agent era, the value of open source becomes even more critical.' Alibaba chairman Joe Tsai framed it in terms of diffusion: only open source enables widespread adoption, and only widespread adoption can create a sustainable, inclusive intelligent era.

> 'Open source may amplify certain composite security problems. DeepSeek is currently using model tiering to constrain some capabilities of open models in order to improve safety.' — Gao Xi, research engineer at DeepSeek, speaking during the Wuzhen Summit

One expo demonstration makes the loop concrete. A robot running Ant LingBot's model can pick up differently packaged medicines in a simulated retail pharmacy, and the system is already deployed in several pharmacies in Shanghai's Pudong district. The LingBot model family supports 17 brands and more than 20 robot configurations, and data fed back during debugging and use feeds the next iteration. What is genuinely scarce here is not a weight file but a deploy–feedback–retrain loop, plus the engineering ability to make heterogeneous hardware share one intelligence layer. The expo, themed 'Intelligent Connectivity, Seeing the Future', brought 671 companies from 54 countries and regions with over 1,000 new technologies and products.
## The other side: a security bill that must be paid together

The 'Frontier AI Safety and Governance 2026: Risk Perception and Collaborative Governance' report, released at the main forum on 3 November, moved the discussion from principles to mechanisms. Issued by the conference's AI special committee, it makes five recommendations: coordinate model safety evaluation, jointly verify safety commitments and their implementation, strengthen incident notification and joint response, improve governance arrangements for agents and open models, and deepen capacity building so safety resources are shared.

Its definition of 'frontier AI' is itself notable: capability is the criterion, with no hard threshold on parameter count or training compute, and agents, multi-agent collaboration and embodied systems are included, focused on large-scale civilian applications. The study finds that misuse and criminal risk, information integrity risk and critical-system risk have already materialised, while societal and structural risks accumulate over time in employment and education. Industry is producing its own instruments in parallel: DeepSeek discussed model tiering to constrain certain open-model capabilities, while MiniMax chief architect Feng Wen noted that open models' defensive capability against network attacks is improving and that deploying them could strengthen overall defence. The same openness is both a diffusion surface for risk and a substrate for defence.
## From consensus to replicable practice

A set of 'Building a Community with a Shared Future in Cyberspace' case studies released during the summit selected 11 practices from more than 360 submissions across over 80 countries and regions, covering cybersecurity, trusted cross-border data governance and open-source collaboration. Tencent senior vice president Xi Dan put the value judgement plainly: developing AI is about amplifying human value and letting AI empower people. GSMA chairman John Hoffman reiterated the summit's long-standing maxim — leave no one behind.
- Judge open source by derivative model counts, vertical penetration and real deployment feedback, not downloads or stars.
- Model tiering, coordinated evaluation and incident notification are becoming the institutional interfaces of an open ecosystem, as important as licence text.
- Compute remained a hard constraint over the past year: when weights are free, compute, data and engineering capability determine the competitive outcome more sharply.
- Governance that stays in a report cannot constrain cross-border deployment; whether it crystallises into replicable practice is the next dividing line.
## Conclusion: scarcity is moving up the stack

Taken together, Wuzhen is not saying 'we open-sourced again'. It is repricing the value chain: foundation models are commoditising, and scarcity is moving up toward compute, toolchains, vertical solutions, service ecosystems and safety governance. For developers and enterprises, the barrier is no longer access to a sufficiently capable model but the ability to place it inside an operable, evaluable and accountable production pipeline. That is also why a summit themed on openness devoted comparable space to a governance report.

Facts and quotations are drawn from public reporting by Xinhua/CCTV, the Economic Information Daily, Renmin University of China and the China Economic News Network; the source link is appended below.

title: 从 53 国零关税到深圳 APEC：11 月这扇「进口窗口」正在改写出海的反向逻辑
summary: 第九届进博会 11 月 5 日至 10 日在上海举行，国家展吸引 69 个国家和国际组织，最不发达国家免费展位面积增加 17%。叠加自 5 月 1 日起对 53 个非洲建交国 100% 税目零关税，以及 11 月 18 日至 19 日的深圳 APEC 领导人会议，这个 11 月释放的不是单一展会红利，而是一组关于「买进来」与「规则接口」的制度信号。
body: 第九届中国国际进口博览会于 11 月 5 日至 10 日在上海举办。据中国网梳理的外媒报道，本届国家展共有 69 个国家和国际组织参展，摩尔多瓦、罗马尼亚、索马里、加蓬、塞舌尔以及联合国开发计划署为首次参展；为服务发展中国家，主办方专门升级亚非产品专区，为最不发达国家提供的免费展位面积增幅达 17%。
把进博会仅当作一场采购展会，会低估它在 2026 年末的位置：自 5 月 1 日起中方对 53 个非洲建交国全面实施 100% 税目产品零关税，展会正成为政策红利转化为实际订单的通道；而 11 月 18 日至 19 日，深圳将举行 APEC 第三十三次领导人非正式会议。进博会、COP31 与 APEC 在同一个月密集排布，构成一组关于市场准入与规则制定的连续窗口。
## 零关税 + 免费展位：从「准入」到「贸易能力建设」
两项安排的性质并不相同。零关税解决的是价格与成本端的准入，免费展位与专区升级解决的是接触成本——对最不发达国家的中小出口商而言，后者往往是更硬的门槛。二者叠加，才让「把政策红利转化为订单」这句话具备可操作的载体。据公开报道，本届开幕式有多国政要出席，加蓬总统、奥地利总理、古巴副总理兼外贸外资部长、斯洛伐克副总理兼经济部长、格鲁吉亚副总理兼经济与可持续发展部长等均在受邀之列。
参展清单能看出诉求的变化。津巴布韦《先驱报》报道，十多家企业参展，展品涵盖园艺农产品、加工食品、皮革制品及其他高附加值制造品；坦桑尼亚派出 36 家企业和机构，带来咖啡、茶叶、蜂蜜等本土特色农产品；肯尼亚主打特色农产品；伊朗德黑兰商会组织的参展企业则重点布局医疗设备、药品、人工智能、先进材料、汽车零部件与消费品。
> 「参展的核心目标是扩大对华出口，推动出口品类摆脱对传统大宗商品的依赖，实现产品多元化。」——津巴布韦贸促会 ZimTrade 首席执行官 Allan Majuru
这句表述比任何规模数字都更值得注意。发展中国家的目标已不只是「多卖一点」，而是把出口结构从单一大宗商品，向加工品、品牌消费品与高附加值制造迁移；坦桑尼亚工业与贸易部副部长 Dennis Londo 也把进博会定位为产品展示、商务洽谈与吸引投资的复合平台。对中国采购方而言，这意味着供给侧的品类与合规要求同时变复杂——原产地规则、检验检疫、冷链与结算，都会比关税本身更决定订单能否落地。
## 「反向出海」：买进来也是全球配置能力

过去几年谈出海，默认语境是把中国商品卖出去。但进博会代表的是另一半能力：把全球供给稳定地组织进中国的生产与消费体系。2025 年中国与 APEC 其他成员货物贸易进出口 26.29 万亿元，占同期中国外贸总值 57.82%；APEC 21 个成员经济体约占全球 GDP 的 60%、全球贸易额的 46%–50%，并吸纳约 56% 的全球 FDI 净流入。在这样的结构里，进口侧的制度化通道与出口侧的渠道能力，其实是同一套全球配置能力的两面。
这也解释了为什么今年密集落地的多是「接口型」成果：2026 年 APEC 贸易部长会议批准了新一期《APEC 创新、有竞争力和韧性的服务业路线图》，《APEC 贸易数字化合作框架》取得实质性进展；数字和人工智能部长会议通过《2026 年 APEC 数字和人工智能部长声明（成都声明）》。这些文本不直接产生订单，却决定订单以什么方式被计价、传输、认证与结算。
## 深圳 APEC：从展示窗口到规则窗口

2026 年是 APEC「中国年」，主题为「建设亚太共同体，促进共同繁荣」，三大优先领域为「开放、创新、合作」，全年预计举办约 300 场活动。这是中国继 2001 年上海、2014 年北京之后第三次担任东道主，领导人非正式会议定于 11 月 18 日至 19 日在深圳举行。10 月 20 日至 21 日首次在香港举行的第 33 届 APEC 财长会，已把数字基础设施融资、普惠金融与公私营合作融资模式纳入议题。
- 对企业而言，11 月的可操作窗口有三段：进博会（5–10 日）看品类与供应商，COP31（9–20 日，安塔利亚）看气候与融资措辞，深圳 APEC（18–19 日）看规则与数字化框架。
- 零关税清单的实际价值取决于原产地证明、标准互认与检验流程，而非税目数量本身；合规能力是红利兑现率的分母。
- 出口结构从大宗商品转向加工品，意味着更长的账期、更细的品控与更重的品牌投入，中小出口商需要的不是展位而是渠道伙伴。
- 对出海服务商，机会正在从「帮中国企业卖出去」扩展到「帮海外供给进得来、留得住」，包括合规、认证、冷链与跨境结算。
## 结语：红利不在展台，在制度接口
把三件事连起来读，进博会提供的是接触面，零关税提供的是价格条件，APEC 提供的是规则环境。真正决定 2026 年末这轮窗口能留下多少增量的，不是签约金额的照片，而是有多少供应商完成了从一次参展到常年供货的转化，以及有多少制度接口被固化为可复用的流程。对做出海的人，这比任何一场展会的头条数字都更值得跟踪。

title: From Zero Tariffs for 53 Nations to Shenzhen APEC: November and the Reverse Logic of Going Global
summary: The ninth China International Import Expo runs from 5 to 10 November in Shanghai, with 69 countries and international organisations in the national exhibition and a 17% increase in free booth space for least-developed countries. Layered on 100% tariff-free treatment for 53 African nations since 1 May and the APEC leaders' meeting in Shenzhen on 18–19 November, the month delivers not one trade-show dividend but a set of institutional signals about importing and rule-making.
body: The ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) takes place in Shanghai from 5 to 10 November. According to a round-up of foreign media reporting by China.com.cn, 69 countries and international organisations joined the national exhibition, with Moldova, Romania, Somalia, Gabon, Seychelles and the UN Development Programme participating for the first time. Organisers upgraded the Asia–Africa product zone and increased free booth space for least-developed countries by 17%.

Treating the CIIE as just another procurement fair understates its position in late 2026. Since 1 May, China has applied zero tariffs across 100% of tariff lines to 53 African countries with diplomatic relations, and the expo has become a channel for converting that policy into actual orders. Then, on 18–19 November, Shenzhen hosts the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting. The CIIE, COP31 and APEC cluster within a single month, forming a continuous window on market access and rule-making.
## Zero tariffs plus free booths: from access to trade capacity

The two arrangements do different work. Zero tariffs address price and cost at the border; free booths and an upgraded zone address the cost of making contact — often the harder barrier for small exporters from least-developed economies. Only together do they give the phrase 'turning policy dividends into orders' an operational vehicle. Public reporting indicates that several foreign leaders attended the opening ceremony, including the presidents of Gabon and the prime minister of Austria alongside deputy prime ministers and economy ministers from Cuba, Slovakia and Georgia.

The exhibitor list reveals how demands are changing. Zimbabwe's The Herald reported more than a dozen companies bringing horticultural produce, processed foods, leather goods and other higher-value manufactured products. Tanzania sent 36 companies and institutions with coffee, tea and honey. Kenya brought speciality agricultural products, while an Iranian delegation organised by the Tehran Chamber of Commerce focused on medical devices, pharmaceuticals, artificial intelligence, advanced materials, auto parts and consumer goods.

> 'The core goal is to expand exports to China and move the export mix away from dependence on traditional commodities toward diversification.' — Allan Majuru, CEO of ZimTrade, Zimbabwe's trade promotion agency

That sentence matters more than any scale figure. The objective is no longer simply to sell more, but to shift the export structure from single commodities toward processed goods, branded consumer products and higher-value manufacturing. Tanzania's Deputy Minister of Industry and Trade Dennis Londo similarly framed the expo as a combined platform for product display, business negotiation and investment attraction. For Chinese buyers, this means both the category mix and the compliance burden get more complex — rules of origin, inspection and quarantine, cold chains and settlement will determine whether an order actually lands, more than the tariff line itself.
## Reverse globalisation: importing is also a capability

For years 'going global' in Chinese business discourse meant selling Chinese goods abroad. The CIIE represents the other half of the capability: organising global supply stably into China's production and consumption system. In 2025, China's goods trade with other APEC members reached 26.29 trillion yuan, 57.82% of its total foreign trade. APEC's 21 member economies account for roughly 60% of global GDP, 46–50% of global trade and about 56% of global FDI net inflows. In that structure, institutional channels on the import side and distribution capability on the export side are two faces of the same allocative capacity.

This also explains why so many of this year's deliverables are interface-shaped. The 2026 APEC Meeting of Ministers Responsible for Trade approved a new APEC Roadmap for Innovative, Competitive and Resilient Services, and substantive progress was made on an APEC Framework for Trade Digitalisation Cooperation. The digital and AI ministers' meeting adopted the 2026 APEC Ministerial Statement on Digital and Artificial Intelligence (Chengdu Statement). None of these texts generates an order directly, but they determine how orders are priced, transmitted, certified and settled.
## Shenzhen APEC: from showcase window to rules window

2026 is APEC's 'China Year', themed 'Building an Asia-Pacific Community for Common Prosperity', with three priorities — openness, innovation and cooperation — and roughly 300 events planned across the year. It is China's third time as host, after Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014, with the leaders' meeting set for 18–19 November in Shenzhen. The 33rd APEC Finance Ministers' Meeting, held for the first time in Hong Kong on 20–21 October, already put digital infrastructure financing, inclusive finance and public–private financing models on the table.

- For businesses, November offers three actionable windows: the CIIE (5–10) for categories and suppliers, COP31 in Antalya (9–20) for climate and finance language, and Shenzhen APEC (18–19) for rules and digital frameworks.

- The real value of a zero-tariff list depends on certificates of origin, standards mutual recognition and inspection procedures, not the number of tariff lines; compliance capacity is the denominator of any dividend.
- A shift from commodities to processed goods implies longer payment cycles, tighter quality control and heavier brand investment; small exporters need channel partners more than booth space.

- For service providers, the opportunity is expanding from 'helping Chinese firms sell out' to 'helping overseas supply get in and stay' — compliance, certification, cold chain and cross-border settlement.
## Conclusion: the dividend is in the interface, not the booth

Read together: the CIIE supplies the contact surface, zero tariffs supply the price condition, and APEC supplies the rules environment. What determines how much of this late-2026 window persists is not the photo of a signing ceremony but how many suppliers convert a single exhibition into year-round supply, and how many institutional interfaces harden into reusable processes. For anyone working in cross-border business, that is worth tracking far more closely than the headline numbers of any trade fair.
